description: The beta-decay coupling s^2 equals [2]_q - [2]_1 exactly, so it is the q-dimension minus its classical value; that pattern motivates the candidate family c*(W - W(1))*bridge for a W-based replacement. The family is EXCLUDED (scope-(b)): s^2 vanishes to second order at q=1 while W - W(1) vanishes to first, and once a bridge repairs the order the ratio still runs (5 -> 695.91 between q=1 and q=2), so no constant rescales one onto the other. Says nothing against W itself.

convention.anchor: proton pin (Q_50_DIGIT_STR); identities exact in q

scope: (b) structural exclusion of the family c*(W - W(1))*X for X in {h, hbar_q, s, q-1, h/2}, by proved non-constancy of the ratio. NOT an exclusion of a W-based coupling of another shape: a ratio against another trace, a Jones-normalised object (V_K(1) = 1 for every knot), or a bar-parity component are untested.

assertions.name: s_sq_equals_two_q_minus_classical_value
assertions.note: s^2 = [2]_q - [2]_1 EXACTLY: the coupling is a classical-value deviation

assertions.name: W_at_one_is_one_quarter
assertions.note: W(1) = 1/4, so W does not vanish classically and W - W(1) is the candidate

assertions.name: W_residual_vanishes_to_first_order
assertions.note: W'(1) = 5 != 0, so W - W(1) is first order — the order mismatch

assertions.name: every_order_matched_bridge_has_leading_coeff_five_times_bridge
assertions.note: leading coeff of (W-1/4)*X is W'(1)*X'(1) = 5*X'(1), never s^2's 1

assertions.name: candidate_ratio_is_not_constant
assertions.note: R(q) runs: 5 as q->1, 8.524 at q0, 65.27 at 3/2, 695.91 at 2 — no normalisation CONSTANT absorbs it (Lean no_constant_rescaling)
